pages/13203.content:

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay=""][vc_column][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3" css=".vc_custom_1728883313202{border: 20px initial !important;}" col_inner_shadow="box_shadow_enable:disable|shadow_horizontal:0|shadow_vertical:15|shadow_blur:50|shadow_spread:0|box_shadow_color:rgba(0%2C0%2C0%2C.35)" col_inner_shadow_hover="box_shadow_enable:disable|shadow_horizontal:0|shadow_vertical:15|shadow_blur:50|shadow_spread:0|box_shadow_color:rgba(0%2C0%2C0%2C.35)"][dfd_heading delimiter_settings="border-bottom-style:solid;|border-bottom-width:1px;|width:50px;|border-bottom-color:#dddddd;" style="style_02" subtitle="If you're into..." title_font_options="tag:h3" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_family:QwigleyRegular"]Arts & Entertainment[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text css=""]

VISUALIZATIONS to AMUSE

This is the "About Oddtoe" section, so I might as well show you around. I like and do a lot of types of art. Some of the favorites are street art, projection art, animation, and installation art. Want to amuse and stir the happy emotions of your audience? Welcome to my world.

Transforming ideas into tangible, breathtaking realities, Oddtoe specializes in 3D design and immersive spatial experiences tailored for private clients and government park planners. This is an artistic craft that brings visions to life through cutting-edge visualization, landscape design, and site-specific installations. Whether designing sculptural outdoor spaces, conceptualizing urban parks, or crafting bespoke private topiary gardens, every project is a fusion of artistic sensibility and technical precision.

For those seeking to push beyond conventional design, immersive experiences offer a new frontier in spatial storytelling. From interactive light installations to topographically inspired 3D sculptures, each piece is meticulously designed to engage and inspire. Government planners and landscape architects benefit from highly detailed visual proposals that communicate complex ideas with clarity, while private clients enjoy bespoke design solutions that reflect their unique aesthetic and spatial needs. Whether shaping a tranquil retreat or a dynamic public space, the focus remains on creating environments that not only serve a purpose but leave a lasting emotional impact.

screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][vc_column_text css=""]Three-dimensional modeling is what sets up the imagery and animation I create as Oddtoe. Dimensional data is the underlying and reusable asset for character designs and background art. What Is It You Do?

I'm a kinetic sculptor, but more in the sense that my kinetic sculpture concepts are featured in a larger experience. Let’s say I’ve imagined a moving 5-metre moving-parts windmill. That Kinetic design, that kinetic windmill will only be a part of what is the total experience. It’s probably in a topiary garden, with a dragonfly robot scheduled to fly around the entire landscape experience. I tend to imagine kinetic sculptures as lending movement, height, and hard materials (metal, stone, composites) into an installation piece.

Why Are You a Kinetic Sculptor, Why Do You Do It?

You mean as opposed to regular or immobile sculpture? Yea, good question. Kinetic movement in sculptures still has some ‘undiscovered’ possibilities. It’s a newer form of sculpture art, so it’s natural the breadth of artist working in the field hasn’t been as large as in your more traditional art forms, like painting or static sculpture. Plus, I think kinetic sculpture is cool. It gets me out of bed, inspired.

What Makes Oddtoe’s Kinetic Sculpture Unique or Different?

For one thing, robotics. Also, movement can start by algorithmic design. Movement to me as Oddtoe can be started by a robot. Introducing machines to an artistic equation creates so many places for creativity. The design of the kinetic system is something I work on now. By the kinetic system, I mean like the system of triggers, actions, and interactions in a Rube Goldberg-sense. How even a George Rhoads, a favorite kinetic sculptor of mine would approach his kinetic systems when he drew up his plans.

What’s Your ‘Perfect’ Kinetic Sculpture Client?

The client certainly has a vision and a means to get there. A client who can see the excitement of what kinetic sculpture can be in the future, see its creative potential inside the installation art world. I can see a couple of ‘perfect clients’ outside the art world, too. The type of large-scale kinetic sculpture that Oddtoe’s geared to design also feature in the business cases of resorts and destination events. So those individual whose business is it to make a name, a brand and are looking to promote real estate or specific location like holiday resort, amusement park, or a public space — those individuals are seeking out creative artists like Oddtoe to work with on exciting physical experiences and art pieces. Last group I could see are event and brand marketers and the creative agencies who work with them. Physical experiences, event experiences are inherently designed to be special, something their audiences want to share — through work of mouth, through social media. The stuff I design as a kinetic sculptor looks good on Instagram, Facebook, on Twitter. These images then travel for these clients. So yea, I think marketers and brands can see the return-on-investment on an immersive or experiential design experience, featuring a kinetic sculpture.

As a Kinetic Sculptor, What’s Your ‘Perfect’ Project?

The sculpture itself is beefy. By ‘beefy’, I mean it it’s substantial in terms of the overall proportion of the art experience I’m creating. If it’s not the main thing you’re fascinated with as a viewer, it’s the second-most thing you’re interested in, perhaps after only a topiary piece or organic focal point I placed in the center. So yea, I put a lot of energy in the physical 3d design phase. So not only is it big, it also has to move or be triggered for movement uniquely. As I mentioned earlier, I think brings computer algorithms and robots into the mix is exciting. So another request I’d have for what would make a kinetic sculpture quote-unquote ‘perfect’ is that I’m using some sort of new technology — a new style robot or using some creative logic for an algorithm which I’d have my staff at Datalabs working on. Automation and algorithms are the future of animated sculpture design. At least, that’s what I think.

What’s the Last Crazy Thing You Thought About Kinetic Sculpture?

Whoa. I have a few. This is where I tend to go in my creative Happy Place. The last crazy thing I thought about kinetic sculpture — a thought that has no real value {laughs} — was around rubber dolls heads. Ha. I saw a great social post about an Irish student’s recall about a ketamine experience gone wrong,. When this author thought to illustrate his or her feelings of drug-induced embarrassment, so he or she attached a photo of a doll head, with its face sucked in, a kind of a shameful facial implosion. I got a belly chuckle out of that image, so I started to imagine a kinetic sculpture experience involving a multitude of rubber doll heads, their faces sucked in and algorithmically distorted with air pressure technology. {laughs} But then that project started looking like the Game of Thrones’ Hall of Many Faces. And then even I got creeped out ! {laughs} So yea, that was my last crazy thought about kinetic sculpture. Still might work on that project though. {laughs}[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="120" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_mobile_spacer_size="80" screen_normal_spacer_size="80" screen_tablet_spacer_size="80"][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/4"][/vc_column][/vc_row]

More comedians, more laughter. And more laughter in the world isn't a bad thing.  I think generative A.I. can help in a positive way to address the current laughter deficit we're experiencing in the 2020s. If our intentions are good.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text]Artist's Statement » In artificial intelligence, there are always permutations, glitches, and odd choices that get made in the stories, poems, and scripts that it creates. [/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_single_image image="12965" img_size="full" alignment="center" onclick="link_image"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3" col_inner_shadow="box_shadow_enable:disable|shadow_horizontal:0|shadow_vertical:15|shadow_blur:50|shadow_spread:0|box_shadow_color:rgba(0%2C0%2C0%2C.35)" col_inner_shadow_hover="box_shadow_enable:disable|shadow_horizontal:0|shadow_vertical:15|shadow_blur:50|shadow_spread:0|box_shadow_color:rgba(0%2C0%2C0%2C.35)"][dfd_icon_list icon_margin="10" icon_bottom_spase="10" icon_color="#f2f2f2" icon_dec_size="100" icon_border_radius="10" icon_border_style="dotted" icon_border_width="2" del_height="1" main_style="style-4" icon_size="35" font_options="line_height:24"][dfd_icon_list_item icon="dfd-icon-robot dfd_icon_set-icon-robot"]

One animator. The full pipeline.

Generative AI animation is only as good as the person directing it. Oddtoe brings twenty years of illustration, motion design, and visual storytelling experience to every frame — AI handles the scale, and a non-boring human handles the design and the judgement. Makes it an easier process for you, the client.

[/dfd_icon_list_item][/dfd_icon_list][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="10" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="10" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][dfd_icon_list icon_margin="10" icon_bottom_spase="10" icon_color="#f2f2f2" icon_dec_size="100" icon_border_radius="10" icon_border_style="dotted" icon_border_width="2" del_height="1" main_style="style-4" icon_size="35"][dfd_icon_list_item icon="dfd-icon-pencil_2 dfd_icon_set-icon-pencil_2"]

Illustration first. Always.

In my career, I have been a political cartoonist, a puppeteer, a data visualizer, and a street artist. But my foundational skill is illustration. Since 2006, Oddtoe has been around the block, working for such organizations such as National Geographic.  

[/dfd_icon_list_item][/dfd_icon_list][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="10" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="10" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][dfd_icon_list icon_margin="10" icon_bottom_spase="10" icon_color="#f2f2f2" icon_dec_size="100" icon_border_radius="10" icon_border_style="dotted" icon_border_width="2" del_height="1" main_style="style-4" icon_size="35"][dfd_icon_list_item icon="dfd-icon-map_way dfd_icon_set-icon-map_way"]

Motion Design for Visual Facts

The integration of generative A.I. with traditional animation is a challenge. The design of non-fiction graphics, maps, and charts for a factual story is a challenge. Feeding the right data to a curiously-talented storyteller that happens to be a "bot"? That is a professional skill. 

[/dfd_icon_list_item][/dfd_icon_list][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="10" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="10" screen_tablet_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="30"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="65" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="65" screen_tablet_spacer_size="55" screen_mobile_spacer_size="45"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_bg_style="canvas" dfd_enable_overlay="" css=".vc_custom_1776498629325{background-color: #332D26 !important;}" dfd_bg_color_value="#332D26"][vc_column][dfd_heading style="style_02" subtitle="Animation that treats the audience as intelligent." title_font_options="tag:h2|font_family:BebasNeueRegular" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_family:QwigleyRegular"]Generative AI Animator in Australia, Outside of Hollywood[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]The animators who work or have worked for Walt Disney all seem to come from Los Angeles. Maybe that's why movie animation all looks the same — either 2d Disney, 3d Pixar. At least, anime has given us new imagery and story types. But Hollywood animation isn't run by animators, but by studio heads who bear the risk for generating original stories and intellectual property (IP). Generative AI changes that equation. A single animator with the right tools and twenty years of animation experience can now produce work that would have required a studio of fifty. That's what Oddtoe offers. Not a cheaper version of the same thing. Something genuinely different.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]The subjects worth animating are rarely the easy ones. Science, history, technology, and deep dives into current events — that's where generative AI animation can help institutions and content creators that couldn't afford or lacked the talent to create beautiful explainers, animated videos, or documentary scenes.  Oddtoe is a generative AI animator. To me, Oddtoe is an animation house that can imagine 100 new animated comedies and kids' movies over breakfast. For ongoing clients, Oddtoe animates for YouTubers, helps influencers explain concepts better, or visualizes academic research in a way that is beyond what a typical university, think tank, or museum staffer could. These are clients who are telling stories that have a positive impact on their audiences; they're both educational and entertaining.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner Interested in a

next-level Comedy Content Creator?

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text item_animation="transition.fadeIn"]

 Oddtoe uses a "hybrid" method for comedy writing. The notepad of ideas, quotes, and funny scenes won't be replaced by generative artificial intelligence (AI) any time soon. AI is in its infancy for joke writing and comedic stories. However, I have included the technology in my workflow and writing process. 

Take a look at the possibilities for both generative AI & my own abilities. (Below: The Oddtoe-written animated comedy series, "Wire Taps", 2023)

This new era will be a step-change evolution." title_font_options="tag:h2|font_family:BebasNeueRegular|color:%23000000|letter_spacing:0" subtitle_font_options="tag:h2|color:%23000000|line_height:20" subheading_margin="margin-bottom:10px;"]A Stream of Comedic Skits & Stories[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/5"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/5"][vc_column_text css=""]The Venn diagram of Oddtoe is visualization, A.I., and humor. Comedy writing is bound to collide with ChatGPT, Claude, and other generative platforms. Thematic structures, plot devices, jokes — there's so much more to experience when an AI can contribute to the writer's room. In addition, I'm interested in new types of stories set in different locations. After all, not every sitcom needs to be made in New York or Los Angeles.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/5"][vc_column_text css=""]Working with generative A.I. is like working with a talented musician who wants to jam with you when you want to. The future is generative humor. And a generative humorist needs to tend to his or her library of comedy data, much like what is used to train an A.I. with the cartoons from the New Yorker.  My personal hope is that, with a personal algorithm and deep knowledge of AI technology,[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="120" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_spacer_size="80" screen_tablet_spacer_size="80"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/5"][vc_column_text css=""]I can trust that my sense of humor is more or less used to train the model. And the stepping stones to building a funny story will gradually build on one another. Gags will progress to comedic scenes and soon to fully-fledged stories that hold together, but generate a new type of comedy writing. Add to the potential to cost-effectively visualize this content, and one can see the fun that's possible to design and animate.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/5"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="340" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="340" screen_tablet_spacer_size="450" screen_mobile_spacer_size="450"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="340" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="340" screen_tablet_spacer_size="240" screen_mobile_spacer_size="190"][vc_column_text]

PROJECTION ART FESTIVALS

This year is showing a strong uptick in evening events, in general, and projection art festivals, specifically. 

Every level of government — local, state, and Federal — is funding the arts bodies and councils. Now that funding is filtering through to the community events that have been so desperately needed, post-pandemic.

Good onya!

More intelligence." title_font_options="tag:h2|font_family:BebasNeueRegular|color:%23000000|letter_spacing:0" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|color:%23000000"]Original Stories Generated by A.I. & the Human Mind[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]The era of multi-disciplinary artists is here. The tools and technology now available to artists and designers are astounding. As Oddtoe, I adore light projection, a little bit of nature — topiary, for instance — and heavy influences from cartooning and children's book illustration. My work is comedic. The visual style is very direct, with unique, detailed characters in full backgrounds. Good typography and textured surfaces also mark my style.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]Oddtoe's typical clients are brands, advertisers, and publishers whose user experience has been dulled by the design's "race to the bottom" (think Canva-style design) — or worse, who've failed to stand out at all. Global brands with room for a more dynamic approach to illustration and animation also tend to gravitate toward "out-there" work. Also, for some reason, individuals, couples, or foundations with money ;) seem more interested in commissioning the most distinctive work. Them them.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="55" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="55" screen_tablet_spacer_size="55" screen_mobile_spacer_size="45"][dfd_button button_text="CONTACT ODDTOE" buttom_link_src="url:https%3A%2F%2Fwww.oddtoe.com%2Fcontact-oddtoe%2F|title:Contact%20Oddtoe" background="#8a8f6a" hover_background="#4e5041" border="border-style:none;|" hover_border="border-style:none;|" title_custom_fonts="font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:700%20bold%20regular%3A700%3Anormal" style="style_6" padding_left="35" padding_right="35" title_font_options="line_height:45" title_google_fonts="yes"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="65" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="65" screen_tablet_spacer_size="65" screen_mobile_spacer_size="65"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][/vc_row]

width="1/4"][vc_column_text]As a visual artist specializing in 3D visualization, garden design, and illustration, the grittier areas of Berlin, Germany are an endless source of inspiration. Certain neighborhoods stand out to me for the art and inspiration: the ever-changing graffiti and street art of Kreuzberg; the eclectic RAW-Gelände of Friedrichshain and its projection art museums;[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text]and the organic, community-driven spirit of Neukölln for innovative garden designs. Whether it's Mitte's historical significance or Schlossgarten Charlottenburg's lovely display of topiary, Berlin provides the perfect canvas for creativity. The city offers one of the most unique blend of history, modernity, and artistic expression in all of Europe.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="120" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_mobile_spacer_size="80" screen_normal_spacer_size="80" screen_tablet_spacer_size="80"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_bg_style="image" dfd_bg_image_new="15239" dfd_bg_image_repeat="no-repeat" dfd_bg_img_attach="fixed" dfd_overlay_color="#322d26" dfd_overlay_pattern="transperant" dfd_row_config="full_width_content" css=".vc_custom_1722432583555{background-position: center !important;background-repeat: no-repeat !important;background-size: cover !important;}"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="60" screen_tablet_spacer_size="50" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="60" screen_tablet_spacer_size="50" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][vc_column_text item_animation="transition.fadeIn"]

Looking to collaborate from

Berlin, JA?

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="10"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="10"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text]As Oddtoe, a visual artist offering visualization, and design services, Berlin and Germany offer boundless opportunities for artistic collaboration. Oddtoe is dedicated to transforming artistic visions into reality, capturing the essence of Berlin’s diverse cultural tapestry. Inspired by the city's renowned museums, such as the Berlinische Galerie, [/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text]Oddtoe reimagines art and design in innovative ways. Germany has always had a great history of design. In that spirit, Oddtoe is dedicated to turning the creative visions of German companies into physical reality, blending the contemporary influences that make Berlin unique. how does using a prop maker who specializes in digital models, generative AI, and 3d printing benefit you? Glad you asked. There are three main benefits: One: What you see is what you'll get. No surprises. This new generation of software modeling and prop construction is the best there is. And Oddtoe will keep you in the loop throughout the design and fabrication process. [/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text]Two: An almost infinite amount of prototypes to see. Not sure exactly what you want? This is where generative AI in 3d modeling really helps out. Oddtoe can output a dozen early images or prototypes. Three: Speed. Because you, whether you're a Prop Master, Set Designer, or Head of Production, are included in the process of prop design from the start, approvals are quicker. This diminishes the need for redesigns. Recently, Hollywood studios like Paramount Pictures, Warner Bros., and Sony Pictures have understood the need to source talent (and tax breaks) from Australia. Steamers like Apple+ and Netflix are also required to secure a portion of their content from the countries where their revenue comes from. This is one of the many reasons prop masters, art directors, and production supervisors are looking Down Under, to Australia for expertise in design, filling job roles with talent with Aussie accents. With a fully digital workflow, cloud-based connectivity, and a[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text]beneficial difference in time zones,  Oddtoe services the North American market, specifically the entertainment industry's epicenter in Los Angeles, California: Hollywood. Domestically, the Australian movie, TV, and advertising industry is thriving. Backed by the Federal government, movie studios in the Docklands, Melbourne, on the Gold Coast in Queensland, and in Sydney, the need for prop makers, animators, and other artists has never been greater. So tap into the talent in Melbourne. For those in LA, you can fly direct — only a 14-hour flight. Questions for the

PROP MAKER?

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_accordion style="style-3" active_section="1" font_size="18" tab_title_google_fonts="yes" tab_title_custom_fonts="font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:700%20bold%20regular%3A700%3Anormal" icon_size="14"][vc_tta_section title="What does a prop designer do?" tab_id="1685677784578-172f9372-59216fce-87a6"][vc_column_text]

A prop designer develops concepts & designs for the props required in the production of a movie, TV show, commercial, or theater performance.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="What do prop makers do?" tab_id="1685677784323-438be9dd-da0e6fce-87a6"][vc_column_text]

Prop makers specialize in creating and constructing props for the entertainment industry. Essentially, they essentially bring the prop designer's concepts to life.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Are there prop makers in Australia?" tab_id="1685677784395-526dd6ff-b9c26fce-87a6"][vc_column_text]

Of course, silly! Prop makers in Australia are particularly prominent in Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, and Adelaide. Here there are heaps of theater companies, movie studios, & production houses. Most Australian prop makers also service events, movie, and TV productions in Asia, the U.S., and Canada, and Europe's entertainment industry in England, France, and Germany (+ others).

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="How is generative AI used in movies?" tab_id="1685677784507-83427dcb-7a756fce-87a6"][vc_column_text]

Generative AI is often used in the early stages of concept and design. Gradually, the use of AI will grow into other areas of TV and movie making, including character design, background art, and animation.

PROJECTION ART FESTIVALS

This year is showing a strong uptick in evening events, in general, and projection art festivals, specifically. 

Every level of government — local, state, and Federal — is funding the arts bodies and councils. Now that funding is filtering through to the community events that have been so desperately needed, post-pandemic.

Good onya!

PROJECTION ARTIST FOR FESTIVALS

The business case for festivals is foot traffic. Local councils want it. Precinct associations want it. Sponsors want it. Projection art pulls crowds into laneways, parks, and main streets after dark — the hours retail and hospitality need most.

Want proof that this type of activation is working? In Australia, night-time pedestrian activity in Melbourne precincts now exceeds pre-pandemic levels, with the sector supporting 31,000 jobs and contributing $3.3 billion to the local economy.

A projection artist for hire is cheaper than a pyrotechnics team, safer than a fireworks permit, and reusable across multiple nights. One commission with Oddtoe. And then multiple activations in a large space, over one night or multiple nights.

That's good business math!

A CONSISTENT ART DIRECTOR

Generative A.I. art is great. However, it does come with limitations. The illustrations it creates are inconsistent. The images are fine for a once-off use. But brands and businesses have longer-term needs and a cohesive style to think about.

[/dfd_icon_list_item][/dfd_icon_list][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="60" screen_tablet_spacer_size="60" screen_mobile_spacer_size="60"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][dfd_icon_list icon_margin="10" icon_bottom_spase="10" icon_color="#f2f2f2" icon_dec_size="100" icon_border_radius="10" icon_border_style="dotted" icon_border_width="2" del_height="1" main_style="style-4" icon_size="35"][dfd_icon_list_item icon="dfd-icon-palette dfd_icon_set-icon-palette"]

A SKILLED ILLUSTRATOR & VISUALIZER

In my career, I have been a political cartoonist, a puppeteer, a data visualizer, and a street artist. But my foundational skill is illustration. Since 2006, Oddtoe has been around the block, working for such organizations such as National Geographic.

AN INTEGRATOR

The integration of generative A.I. art into content production is a massive challenge. How will one artist integrate generative AI into their workflows? How will the I.T. scale with different machine-learning algorithms?

For better or for worse, generative AI is the impact that has hit professional illustration. I'm choosing to use it and ride where my illustration style takes the next few years of work. I have to say I am impressed — impressed with the impact it's having on parts of an illustrator's workflow: on ideation, world-building, and art direction, in particular. This age of generative AI will evolve artists quickly. And new illustration "gods" will come from the disruption.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text]This disruptive technology has accelerated the scale of illustrations produced per year. — And it's all "hockey stick" growth from here out... But notice this: how many illustrations on Midjourney have you seen in your favorite start-up's branding? How about for your supermarket's advertising? Brands and businesses need to think about how they can create new imagery styles — and leave behind the gaudy era of business stock photography once and for all. Who hires a muralist?

Some of the people who hire muralists are government councils, tourist bureaus, property managers, restaurants, schools, or retail stores. A muralist is hired by those who want to beautify their property or by those who want to create a specific mood.   A muralist's job is to bring clients' ideas to life using color, space, and design. A good muralist will be able to work within a budget and produce great results with minimal supervision. However, while working on a project, if there are changes in the client's wishes or the scope of works expands unexpectedly, they may have to return with extra charges for the change in order to meet the client's expectations.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" How do you choose a muralist?

The best way to be sure that you'll get good results from your muralist is to ask for references or recommendations and check them out thoroughly before hiring one. A good candidate will have experience, great ideas, and a portfolio of works done before. And if you're hiring someone for the first time, ensure that they know their responsibilities clearly, so there'll be no issues regarding payment or delays on projects.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]

Muralist for Painting Murals on Walls, Buildings, and Farm Silos

Painting murals on walls, buildings, and farm silos is a specialized job that takes years to master. The problem with muralists today is that they're specialized enough in their chosen mediums. They can't do everything from scratch, which means you have to hire multiple people to get things done right. This leads to delays and cost overruns for clients. Oddtoe offers a comprehensive package of services at an affordable price point so you don't have to worry about hiring multiple contractors or dealing with the headache of managing them all at once.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]

The Proud History of Muralists in Australia

Australia punches above its weight in the art world. And street artists and muralists lead the way. Thankfully, there's a supportive culture at the Federal, State, and Council levels for large-scale commissions. A few well-known mural projects and councils in Australia come to mind: the King Street Murals, St. George Football Club, the Kings Cross Community Centre. Inner West Council, Wollongong Council, City of Melbourne, and the City of Sydney. In addition, the Silo Art Trail project is a shining example of how rural councils have found the power of murals to activate country town's cultures and economies. Oddtoe designs characters with a sketch. Or several. The tools for designing characters are simply a pencil and a glorious blank sheet of note paper. Designing characters has changed so much in the past twenty years. Digital tools are certainly embedded now in a character designer's process. Think: Adobe Illustrator, Photoshop, Procreate. Think of scanners and 3d printers. And now let's drop in the 'most controversial elephant in the room': generative AI.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text]Personal influences of mine are Winsor McCay, Walt Disney, Charles Schulz, or Bill Waterson: a great cartoon character is a great personality, designed to be a part of a wider story. These illustrated or animated characters are the actors in their plays. Hollywood also asks them to be intellectual property (IP) and to be the next thing to entertain us across movies, TV, and video games. width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text]Oddtoe specializes in 2d and 3d character design. I love a detailed brief. I'll take a mood board or other character sheets. And of course, a script is perfect to discover how a character is portrayed in writing. I've got a style for the design of characters. Realism isn't my thing; big heads are. Have a look through my portfolio and you'll get a sense of the style of character designs I like to conjure up. Once I've settled on a character's[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text] physical design, I'll often return to the drawing board. Settling for a Disney or Pixar cookie-cutter character isn't going to happen on my watch, so I often add more detail and uniqueness to any second draft. I want to avoid visual clichés. Villains and the main protagonists of a story often get finer attention and here I often take on influences from other artists. First, as inspiration. Second, to make sure I'm designing a character that's unlike anyone else out there.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="55" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="55" screen_tablet_spacer_size="55" screen_mobile_spacer_size="45"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_delimiter delimiter_style="dfd-delimiter-with-icon" icon_size="15" delimiter_border_style="dotted" icon_fontawesome="fas fa-question-circle" show_icon="enable_icon"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row dfd_enable_overlay="" css=".vc_custom_1690353985120{background-color: #c6acb6 !important;}"][vc_column width="1/4"][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/2"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text item_animation="transition.fadeIn"]

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_accordion style="style-4" active_section="1" font_size="18" tab_title_google_fonts="yes" tab_title_custom_fonts="font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:700%20bold%20regular%3A700%3Anormal" icon_size="14" tab_text_color="#000000"][vc_tta_section title="Can I see more examples of Oddtoe's character designs?" tab_id="1685677784578-172f9372-59216fce-87a6"][vc_column_text]

Absolutely. I think the best place to see my character design style is to check out my panel comics on Instagram.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="What type of projects does Oddtoe work on?" tab_id="1685677784323-438be9dd-da0e6fce-87a6"][vc_column_text]

Books, web series comics, video games, and projects where the character designer is part of a larger production like animated TV shows and movies.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Who are the best types of characters to design in your job?" tab_id="1685677784395-526dd6ff-b9c26fce-87a6"][vc_column_text]

The juicier characters are the stupid ones, the over-the-top characters, villains, nerds, the overly vain characters, and the ones that have a bizarre way of looking at the world. It's not hard to get into those.

WHAT IS A ROBOTICIST?

[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text]In an era defined by technological advancements, the role of a roboticist has gained prominence. But what exactly is a roboticist? Simply put, a roboticist is a professional specializing in designing, developing, and operating robots. These individuals possess a unique blend of computer science, engineering, and artificial intelligence skills. Roboticists create robots for various applications, from manufacturing and healthcare to space exploration and entertainment. They work with cutting-edge technology, such as machine learning and sensor systems, to imbue robots with intelligence and autonomy. But for me, a creative roboticist is whatever I’d like to make it. A far more firm definition will soon be applied to this field of art.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_heading content_alignment="text-left" delimiter_settings="border-bottom-style:dotted;|border-bottom-width:1px;|width:100px;|border-bottom-color:#d2d2d2;" delimiter_margin="margin-top:30px;margin-bottom:0px;" title_google_fonts="yes" title_custom_fonts="font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:700%20bold%20regular%3A700%3Anormal" subtitle_google_fonts="yes" subtitle_custom_fonts="font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic" style="style_01" title_font_options="tag:h3" subtitle_font_options="tag:div|font_size:14" heading_margin="margin-bottom:10px;"]

A ROBOTICIST's Process

Yes, form and function and all that. But now the process goes, hand-in-hand, with a robot — a generative AI bot to create what I create.

[/dfd_icon_list_item][/dfd_icon_list][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="65" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="65" screen_tablet_spacer_size="55" screen_mobile_spacer_size="45"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_bg_style="image" dfd_parallax_style="dfd_vertical_parallax" dfd_bg_image_new="36" dfd_bg_image_size="initial" dfd_parallax_sense="80" css=".vc_custom_1596890262715{background-color: #252525 !important;}"][vc_column width="1/4" dfd_column_responsive_enable="dfd-column-responsive-enable" responsive_styles="padding_left_mobile:20|padding_right_mobile:20"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="80" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_spacer_size="60" screen_tablet_spacer_size="50"][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/2"][dfd_delimiter delimiter_style="dfd-delimiter-with-text" text_delimiter="Ideas as a Designer" title_font_options="font_style_bold:1"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text]

Do You Work With Other Roboticists?

Robotics is moving so fast. Much faster than the art world. Oddtoe is there to catch the wake, so to speak, of the incredible work of the robotics community. To work alongside as humanity takes its best guess about how to work with these things. A creative roboticist isn’t the most important cog in this wheel, but I don’t see anyone else looking at making fun of robots, finding ways to let humans feel one last bit of superiority before the machines take our jobs and become our intimate partners ;).

 

What’s the Perfect Piece?

A robot is at the core of the idea. In itself, the robot is so interesting and intricate that I just need to imagine how it could be better, more interesting, how I can bring out features in the robot to the viewer. Could I place the robot in a different setting? Augment it somehow? Color or adorn it? What other forms can be brought to the party — projected light, kinetic sculpture, digital art?

 

What Idea Do I Want the Viewer to Have?

This is my favorite part of the creative process. Robots conjure up so much in the human mind: fascination, curiosity, fear, and I’d like to explore humor. Humor is a circuit breaker and let’s other deeper ideas possible once the viewer has let down their guard. It’s here that exciting possibilities exist, not all of which I can control as an artist. But I love that. Individuals will have individual takes on what I created and what I meant to convey.

That frees me up to not to have a point to my art ;)

[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text item_animation="transition.slideDownIn"][/vc_column_text][vc_column_text css=""]Shaving shrubs into impossible shapes, blending greenery with metal, masonry, and robots, Oddtoe is an extreme topiarist, a creative botanist and landscape designer — all-in-one. Central to his art practice, Oddtoe’s topiary garden designs incorporate sculpture and projected light and animation into unique landscapes to achieve an awe-inspiring, 'I haven’t seen this before’ effect. “I think uniqueness is important. I’m not here to create a rip-off Versailles garden. To me, an Oddtoe garden is whole new experience, a sensory garden. getting as many senses as possible — sight, sound, smell — on their tippy-toes and begging to know what’s around the next tree." I see gardens as immersive experiences. THE RESORTS & SPAS WITH THE BEST TOPIARIST WINS

World-class resorts around the world are looking for points of difference for their gardens. Increasingly, these resorts are locations where their guests can wander, get lost (both physically and mentally), and can unwind. Zen gardens, if you will. Zen gardens can be quirky. Meditate with humour, I say. My favourite ingredients for a meditative space are plants, light, sound, and creatures (still or kinetic sculptures). The full sensory packet, but designed in a beautifully subtle way. Zen gardens are designed to mollify the mind. Here, auditory design becomes a key ingredient in my practice. Waterfalls, natural sounds — putting together a soundtrack for a garden experience is such a joy for a sensory designer.  

The Case for Extreme Topiary in the Age of Social Media

" In the age of social media, holiday resorts, museums, city gardens, and large-scale real estate developments are all looking for that extra edge, a visual something that gets a visitor to take that smartphone out of their pocket and snap a picture. A garden design to enhance well-being is a start. But a garden design needs to be more. Today, it's got to be bigger than life. It needs to be awe-inspiring.   [/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/6"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/6"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="2/3"][vc_column_text css=""]

The Landscape Design Process for a Top Topiarist

Whether it’s for a museum piece, a holiday resort, or for a private garden, Oddtoe creates innovative landscapes using the same creative process he devised for graphic design, data visualization, and 3d illustration. Visual research followed by sketch work then a phase he calls “doubtful cliff jumps”. “I ask myself how I can push the envelope in a particular field. I may not use a particular plant or design - it may be impossible. But I need to imagine something, however implausible. If it’s landscape design, for me, topiary starts it off. I think in shapes. Ways to create a moment of intrigue in what’s being seen and experienced. A good topiarist knows geometry. A great topiarist knows psychology!"  

A Topiary Designer for Private Gardens

Topiary for a country house, holiday home, or public park, an Oddtoe garden experience can activate a dormant plot of land and transform it into a three-dimensional, organic piece of art. With Oddtoe, plant science can be combined with data science; digital art can be projected upon a gorgeous landscape. To achieve something unique for your property, think of a garden experience designer who works in botany, industrial fabrication, lighting, and digital arts.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer I love non-fiction, data visualization, & animated storytelling. I beg for more graphics whenever I watch documentaries, which is quite a bit. Animated maps, ways to visualize time and place, conceptual diagrams, crime reports, newspaper clippings — the visual library for a documentary animator is enormous. Our guide to what is generative AI animation covers how generative tools widen it further.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text]With a background in interactive design for kids at National Geographic, I now design data and stories for documentaries and for web series content. — factual, but also enjoyablely creative as to how they unfold. Facts are scenes in meticulously crafted shorts, helping the documentary present important information. Cinematography and illustration are combined and designed to make you see data in a way that’s not only understandable but downright pleasing. The visuals don’t just complement the content; they can elevate it, making even the most ordinary facts feel fun to discover. Think of scenes in your head: Page through a vintage scrapbook, where [/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css=""]animated illustrations, newspaper clippings, or crime reports visualize key points in your documentary This isn’t just about throwing graphics on a screen; it’s about having a 'go' at reimagining storytelling. Whether it’s a documentary that dives deep into complex events or a web series that uncovers hidden stories, I like how animation can add a new layer of depth and intrigue. I design data, scene explainers, and conceptual diagrams of all types. Information in motion that is not just understandable, but also oddly captivating.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay=""][vc_column width="1/4"][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/2"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][vc_column_text item_animation="transition.fadeIn"]

Questions about

Documentary animation?

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_accordion style="style-3" active_section="1" font_size="18" tab_title_google_fonts="yes" tab_title_custom_fonts="font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:700%20bold%20regular%3A700%3Anormal" icon_size="14"][vc_tta_section title="What types of animation should documentary filmmakers think about?" tab_id="1685677784395-526dd6ff-b9c26fce-87a64dfd-367f1ddc-0240"][vc_column_text css=""]

Be open-minded as to what style of visualizations could work within your film. See possibilities, different styles, and new visual influences. At the end of the day, this is my expertise inside your film — a team tasked with telling the visual story.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="What type of projects does Oddtoe work on?" tab_id="1685677784323-438be9dd-da0e6fce-87a64dfd-367f1ddc-0240"][vc_column_text css=""]

I love reading non-fiction books. Personally, I like science, biographies, and geography, especially how it relates to people. But it's all good, to be honest.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="Can I see more examples of Oddtoe's animation style?" tab_id="1685677784578-172f9372-59216fce-87a64dfd-367f1ddc-0240"][vc_column_text css=""]

Oddtoe is an artist, a generative AI animation studio and experiential design practice based in Melbourne, Australia. Partnering with cultural institutions, documentary filmmakers, agencies, and event producers worldwide, he works on razor-thin margins, creating everything from exhibition films and branded animation to physical installations and live experiences. See our brand activation ideas.

STORYTELLING for SERIOUS SUBJECTS

Oddtoe creates documentary animation and exhibition films for cultural institutions, universities, and independent producers. Oddtoe is an animator of non-fiction narratives. And with the innovative power of generative AI in the hands of an experienced illustrator, your museum explainer or documentary graphics can take on a whole new life.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_button button_text="Institutions & Filmmakers »" buttom_link_src="url:%23institutions" background="#8a8f6a" hover_background="#4e5041" border="border-style:none;|" hover_border="border-style:none;|" title_custom_fonts="font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:700%20bold%20regular%3A700%3Anormal" style="style_6" padding_left="35" padding_right="35" title_font_options="font_size:18|line_height:45" title_google_fonts="yes"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="55" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="55" screen_tablet_spacer_size="55" screen_mobile_spacer_size="45"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][dfd_heading delimiter_settings="border-bottom-style:solid;|border-bottom-width:1px;|width:50px;|border-bottom-color:#dddddd;" style="style_02" subtitle="The best visual content creator..." title_font_options="tag:h3" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_family:QwigleyRegular"]For Agencies & Brands[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text css=""]

ATTENTION-GRABBING CREATIVE for SCREENS

Oddtoe is a generative AI animator and character designer for agencies and brands with complex stories to tell. From explainer films, video advertisements, to branded content, the workflow starts with illustration and ends with animation that looks eye-catching and seamless rather than generated. Bring your brief — the stranger the better. [/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_button button_text="Agencies & Brands »" buttom_link_src="url:%23agencies" background="#8a8f6a" hover_background="#4e5041" border="border-style:none;|" hover_border="border-style:none;|" title_custom_fonts="font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:700%20bold%20regular%3A700%3Anormal" style="style_6" padding_left="35" padding_right="35" title_font_options="font_size:18|line_height:45" title_google_fonts="yes"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="55" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="55" screen_tablet_spacer_size="55" screen_mobile_spacer_size="45"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][dfd_heading delimiter_settings="border-bottom-style:solid;|border-bottom-width:1px;|width:50px;|border-bottom-color:#dddddd;" style="style_02" subtitle="Let's get physical..." title_font_options="tag:h3" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_family:QwigleyRegular"]For Events & Live Experiences[/dfd_heading][vc_column_text css=""]

From concept renders to working with fabricators, come for the full creative process under one roof. Like previous conference lists here on Oddtoe, this year's guide keeps two things in mind: a great festival culture for attendees and a top-notch professional experience for animators, animation agents, and animation industry folks looking to network with the elite decision-makers. The best animation conferences come from all over the globe and span the entire calendar year.[/vc_column_text][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text css_animation="bounceIn" css=""]However, you'll notice two clusters. Europe dominates. And April and October are always conference- and festival-heavy. When I see the animators and best animation shorts in their respective festival agendas, I mention them in the conference profiles. Some of the greats are back promoting their movies, characters, and sometimes studios. In this 2026 - 2027 guide, I'll also mention — where relevant — how generative AI animation is treated in the festival. Stuttgart International Festival of Animated Film (ITFS)

May 6th to the 10th, 2026 — Stuttgart, Germany (Onsite and virtual) Founded in 1982, ITFS as it is known is Germany's premier animation conference and festival. It always delivers a great experience. See what ITFS has in store for us in its 2026 festival (click). Like some of the other festivals on this list, Stuttgart's offering has now expanded its definitions of animated film. Since 2023, ITFS has offered film screenings, exhibitions, lectures, workshop talks, master classes, and VR events, in addition to a few animated live performances. I love the game center and especially the communal Open Air cinema in the heart of the conference city. There's nothing like having the full backing of your host city for the animated arts. And Stuttgart International Festival of Animated Film sure gets it with its jumbotron cinema set outside in a city square for daily screenings of kids' films and more adult animation in the evenings. So cool. The 2026 conference focus is silhouette animation, marking the 100th anniversary of Lotte Reiniger's The Adventures of Prince Achmed, the oldest surviving animated feature film (1926).[/vc_column_text][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][dfd_delimiter delimiter_style="dfd-delimiter-with-line" delimiter_border_style="dashed"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="2/3"][vc_column_text css=""]

Pictoplasm Berlin

May 7th to the 10th, 2026 — Berlin, Germany (onsite and virtually) Let's go to Germany for the spring and head to the capital for an art experience that only Berlin can deliver. Crossing the Atlantic for our next animation conference, finally, the States puts up an offering — and judging by its artist invite list for 2026 — Pictoplasma Berlin is quite an offering. Take a look at the speaker list: Conor Kehelly, Jun Ioneda, & Melissa Mathieson (+ more.) I like the vibe of the conference curation. The artists are front and center on the website and in the programming. And the animated shorts and featured films that are screening this year are fantastically 'out there' and unlike the safe, vanilla screenings showing at some other festivals. As Pictoplasma themselves say, the animations are "full of psychedelic eye candy, virtual popcorn, and ingenious storytelling." Love it. Annecy Festival

June 21st to the 27th, 2026 — Annecy, France (onsite and virtually) No surprise. My top pick for the best animation conference in the world is the Annecy Festival. Or the Festival d'Annecy. Or the more wordy Annecy International Animation Film Festival and Market. This is the conference every lover of animation should attend at least once in his or her lifetime. Why? It's the world's largest event dedicated to animation. It's in a lovely part of France. It's where the next generation of animators gets their break. And it's an experience like no other. When animation is placed on such a pedestal, as only the French can do, you can only be swept away. The Annecy Festival has been going on for 60 years. The 2026 edition will have it all: massive screenings of top-tier animation, workshops, and the Mifa, one the world's best places to do business both in person and virtually. If you've only got one event, put this animation conference on your schedule.[/vc_column_text][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][vc_zigzag color="chino" el_width="30"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" disable_element="yes" css=".vc_custom_1777606697048{background-color: #0f111b !important;}"][vc_column][dfd_heading module_animation="transition.fadeIn" delimiter_style="icon" icon_size="32" style="style_01" icon="dfd-icon-calendar" title_font_options="tag:h3" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3" heading_margin="margin-top:20px;"]
