MIPJUNIOR 2026

October 10th & 11th, 2026 — Cannes, France (onsite and virtual) Brush up on your French, practice your pitch and your handshake, and head to the South of France where the Who's Who of the animation industry go to make deals. The first of the two 'MIP" conferences runs for three days in October. MIPJUNIOR, as the conference name suggests, is known for its festival screenings of children's programming, including kids' animation. Go for the screenings but stay for the co-production market. Walt Disney, Jim Henson Productions, and Gaumont are just a few of the major studios that will be there. This conference and its big brother, MIPCOM, mean serious business. If you have an animation project to pitch and you have the ability to be in Cannes, you should make the journey. If you're a fan of sunny beaches, animated shorts, and frenzied media executives on their mobile phones, you should make the trip, too.[/vc_column_text][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][dfd_single_image image="13950" image_size="custom" image_width="300" image_height="300" hover_style="dfd-image-scale" link_object="link" image_border_radius="10" enable_link="yes" image_ext_link_url="https://www.mipjunior.com/en-gb.html"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][dfd_delimiter delimiter_style="dfd-delimiter-with-line" delimiter_border_style="dashed"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][dfd_single_image image="13949" image_size="custom" image_width="300" image_height="300" hover_style="dfd-image-scale" image_border_radius="10"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="2/3"][vc_column_text css=""]

MIPCOM Cannes 2026

October 12th to the 15th, 2026 — Cannes, France (onsite and virtual) France again shows its strength on the animation conference circuit. MIPCOM is quite simply where you want to be, whether to strike a business deal for your animated property or gain a foothold in the TV industry. The heart of the conference is the Co-Production Market. The market has a 1000-square-meter theater and a huge networking space.  This is where co-production partnerships are explored, and financing deals are often done. What animation gets seen around the world is often talked about in what is known as the Seaview Producers Hub. A few standouts from this upcoming conference: the MIP AI Exchange which bills itself as a meeting of AI, production, and IP. Check out the sessions directory — the industry names and creative topics alone will make you book your flight![/vc_column_text][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][dfd_delimiter delimiter_style="dfd-delimiter-with-line" delimiter_border_style="dashed"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][dfd_single_image image="13951" image_size="custom" image_width="300" image_height="300" hover_style="dfd-image-scale" image_border_radius="10"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="2/3"][vc_column_text css=""]

View Conference 2026

October 12th to the 16th, 2026 — Torino, Italy (onsite and virtual) Ok. This is animation conference is something. Looking at the speakers' list in the past, it made my Top 4 list two times in the past 5 years. Henry Selnick headlined in 2023. Joaquim Dos Santos, Director of Spider-man: Across the Spider-verse, was there. Netflix Animation, Paramount Animation. Sony. You get the picture. Hearing from these top names is one thing. The View Conference also delivers on other fronts, too. There are seminars on Procreate, Unreal Engine, on VFX. Workshops on Storytelling, and concept art. In 2026, this is the current speaker list, and it's growing. What's not to like about View? As a serious animator, the View Conference is a must-attend once in your life. Wedge it between the MIP conferences in Cannes. (Or do as I plan to do, and attend virtually in my pajamas.)[/vc_column_text][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][vc_zigzag color="chino" el_width="30"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" css=".vc_custom_1693286444868{background-color: #0f111b !important;}"][vc_column][dfd_heading module_animation="transition.fadeIn" delimiter_style="icon" icon_size="32" style="style_01" icon="dfd-icon-calendar" title_font_options="tag:h3|color:%23000000" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3" heading_margin="margin-top:20px;"]

November 2026

[/dfd_heading][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column][vc_column][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="2/3"][vc_column_text css=""]

Manchester Animation Festival

November 8th to the 12th, 2026 — Manchester, England (onsite and virtual) I haven't talked about awards, but if seeing yourself on the red carpet, especially at the Oscars, is important, then you'll want to be aware of the Manchester Animation Festival. MAF (as it's known) has recently become an Academy Award-qualifying festival. Win here, and you're in the running for a golden statue at the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences' premier award ceremony. This is the UK’s largest animation conference. It gets a cadre of high-level companies in attendance, including Aardman Animations, Blue Zoo, ILM, Locksmith Animation, Passion Pictures, and Walt Disney Animation Studios. A simple look at this animation conference's winners' list and you can see the quality from the UK-based animators.[/vc_column_text][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][dfd_single_image image="13941" image_size="custom" image_width="300" image_height="300" hover_style="dfd-image-scale" image_border_radius="10"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][dfd_delimiter delimiter_style="dfd-delimiter-with-line" delimiter_border_style="dashed"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="2/3"][vc_column_text css=""]

Adobe Max

November 10th to the 12th, 2026 — Miami, Florida, U.S.A. (onsite and virtual) This is a big animation conference if you're an After Effects user. And Adobe puts on quite an event! With conference tracks for 3D, illustration, motion design, and, of course, AI, Adobe Max has a lot of content for any animator. Workshops form the basis of the conference, and expert talks from artists and agency heads make this conference different from all the other conferences on this list. There are new speakers every year. The Adobe clan is well-represented. But a few top notch animators working in motion graphics are already on the speaking roster. In 2026, I'm interested in seeing if Adobe's AI (Firefly and Sensei) make it deeper into After Effects. If you're looking for the next big technique or technical breakthrough in the animation industry, this conference is a probable place to learn about it first.[/vc_column_text][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][dfd_single_image image="14372" image_size="custom" image_width="300" image_height="300" hover_style="dfd-image-scale" image_border_radius="10"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][vc_zigzag color="chino" el_width="30"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" css=".vc_custom_1693286454338{background-color: #0f111b !important;}"][vc_column][dfd_heading module_animation="transition.fadeIn" delimiter_style="icon" icon_size="32" style="style_01" icon="dfd-icon-calendar" title_font_options="tag:h3|color:%23000000" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3" heading_margin="margin-top:20px;"]

December 2026

[/dfd_heading][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column][vc_column width="2/3"][vc_column_text css=""]

SIGGRAPH ASIA 2026

December 3rd to the 6th, 2026 — Kuala Lumpur (in-person & virtual) SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 is in Malaysia for the first time. What I like about this conference is its focus: it is not solely on animation. But it is geared toward those who are "excited by research, science, art, animation, gaming, interactivity, education, and emerging technologies." The reason for attending is simple: What gets presented here this year are the technical innovations you'll be experimenting with next year. So get a leg-up and put yourself in a seat (or a virtual environment) for the 3-day conference. This conference has the widest spread of offerings — take a look at the submissions categories and you'll get a sense of the topics, courses, and films you'll see at Asia's best computer graphics and technology festival.[/vc_column_text][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/3"][dfd_single_image image="14381" image_size="custom" image_width="300" image_height="300" hover_style="dfd-image-scale" image_border_radius="10"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column][vc_column][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][vc_zigzag color="chino" el_width="30"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" css=".vc_custom_1693286498701{background-color: #0f111b !important;}"][vc_column][dfd_heading module_animation="transition.fadeIn" delimiter_style="icon" icon_size="32" style="style_01" icon="dfd-icon-calendar" title_font_options="tag:h3|color:%23000000" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3" heading_margin="margin-top:20px;"]

February 2027

[/dfd_heading][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column][vc_column][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][dfd_single_image image="13944" image_size="custom" image_width="300" image_height="300" hover_style="dfd-image-scale" image_border_radius="10"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="3/4"][vc_column_text css=""]

Anima — The Brussels International Animation Film Festival

February/March, 2027 (to be announced) — Brussels, Belgium (in-person & virtual) Happy New Year! 2027 kicks off in Brussels. Anima is in its 46th year, an impressive feat for an animation conference. But you can see why. The level of talent in Belgium and who this festival attracts internationally is second to none. No live-action animation, though. Anima focuses on animation created frame by frame, which can be traditional animated cartoons, stop-motion puppetry, or hand-animated plasticine models. Anima is one of the few animation conferences in the world that is qualified to nominate its winning candidates for the Oscar® for best animated short film.[/vc_column_text][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][vc_zigzag color="chino" el_width="30"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" css=".vc_custom_1693286198732{background-color: #0f111b !important;}"][vc_column][dfd_heading module_animation="transition.fadeIn" delimiter_style="icon" icon_size="32" style="style_01" icon="dfd-icon-calendar" title_font_options="tag:h3|color:%23000000" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3" heading_margin="margin-top:20px;"]

April 2027

[/dfd_heading][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column][vc_column][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][dfd_single_image image="13938" image_size="custom" image_width="300" image_height="300" hover_style="dfd-image-scale" image_border_radius="10"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="3/4"][vc_column_text css=""]

The Art Department Eindhoven 2027

April, 2027? (Dates to be confirmed) — Eindhoven, Netherlands (onsite and virtually) Let's stay in the Benelux region for this creative conference: The Art Department conference celebrates concept art, design and craftsmanship in the film, animation, and games industries. Artist talks are my favourite, and the Art Department has had a wide array of artists types: creature FX artists (Gustav Hoegen), whimsical illustrators (Beatrice Blue), art directors (Dani Dietz), and film directors (Mascha Halberstad), just to name a few. This really is a festival — experience the outdoor expos, the art market, and workshops, along with the fabulous screenings of the best animation. The 2026 version of this festival merged the Berlin conference into the Dutch version. Expect an even bigger festival in 2027.[/vc_column_text][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][dfd_delimiter delimiter_style="dfd-delimiter-with-line" delimiter_border_style="dashed"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="2/3"][vc_column_text css=""]

Cardiff Animation Festival 2027

April, 2027? (Dates to be confirmed) — Cardiff, Wales (onsite and virtual) While not the biggest animation conference on this list, the Cardiff Animation Festival (CAF) is one of the best curated. The style of curation and the character design in the selected animations and illustrations made me take notice and enticed me to see what CAF is all about. The list of the animated shorts in the festival puts it on this guide of the best animation conferences. Have a look and know that if you can't make it to Cardiff in April, you should check out the animators and their submitted works. I can see many of them featuring again and again at other festivals, making CAF a certain tastemaker for up-and-coming animators and those with a distinctive style of visual storytelling[/vc_column_text][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][dfd_single_image image="13953" image_size="custom" image_width="300" image_height="300" hover_style="dfd-image-scale" image_border_radius="10"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][vc_zigzag color="chino" el_width="30"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" css=".vc_custom_1693286301205{background-color: #0f111b !important;}"][vc_column][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][dfd_heading style="style_01" heading_margin="margin-bottom:10px;" title_font_options="tag:h5" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3"]

In 2026 & 2027, What Other Animation Conferences Are You Interested In?

[/dfd_heading][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][vc_column_text css=""]As you can see, lots of movements on the conference calendar. Annecy got bumped off its traditional early-June slot by the G7 Summit and now runs 21–27 June 2026, while Cardiff (23–26 April) has drawn a line in the sand by banning generative-AI films from its 2026 competition. SIGGRAPH Asia heads to Kuala Lumpur for the first time on 1–4 December, expanding the conference's Asian footprint into a new market. And Adobe MAX has packed up its Los Angeles base for the Miami Beach Convention Center, 10–12 November. Am I missing a better animation convention, conference, or festival than the ones above? Contact me and let me know. I'll look to update the animation conference list throughout the year. Are you an animator? Who are the Best Animation Agents & Talent Firms

Working in the Industry Today?

[/dfd_heading][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row css=".vc_custom_1696657787022{background-color: #edb39f !important;}"][vc_column][ultimate_spacer height="30" height_on_tabs="30" height_on_tabs_portrait="30" height_on_mob_landscape="30" height_on_mob="30"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][vc_column_text css_animation="bounceIn" css=""]

Looking for representation for you and your animation? Wanting an advocate for an animated work in Hollywood? Or do you want to become an animation agent yourself? Then check out this year’s guide to the top animation agents in the world.

Not surprisingly, the vast majority of animation agents at the pinnacle are based in and around Los Angeles, California. And quite a few work down the hall from each other inside the same talent agencies. Sharing client rosters and co-pitching properties, the stand-out agency is no surprise to anyone who reads the animation industry news: United Talent Agency or UTA comes in as the top animation agency in the world. 

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][vc_column_text css_animation="bounceIn" css=""]

Boasting the “only dedicated animation” division, UTA knows something good is happening in the animation space.

In 2026, UTA agents working in animation signed deals with big studios such as Disney, Warner Bros., and Sony Pictures. In years past, talent from the UTA rosters has been involved in the great animation blockbusters of the early 21st century.

Independent animation agents certainly have stood their ground and put their case to be included on this current year’s list. Similar to our last list, we have a broad array of talent — nine agents from 9 seperate agencies. This is reflective of an expanding and changing landscape — animation agents that have split out, creating new firms. [/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][vc_column_text css_animation="bounceIn"]

Not really an animator? But you do work in the animation industry? No worries. Some animation agents work in voice talent. Others represent writers, directors, and the technical crews that staff our favorite movies and TV shows. Check out the list below for agents dealing in Hollywood's voice-over work.

So get your animated showreel ready, dust off your pitch bibles, and see who’s made this year’s list of the world’s top animation agents.

Without further ado, here are my picks for the animation animation agents & talent firms of the year. »[/vc_column_text][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" Anna Berthold

  When your job title has the word 'animation' in it and you work at a major talent agency, you're sure to appear on this list. But Anna Berthold tops this year's animation agent list on merits and work rate alone. Leading UTA's animation division, Anna was instrumental in establishing Happy Nest, a joint venture between UTA and Stampede. Happy Nest is now a production company for animated kids and family content. Representing at least 19 clients working heavily in the animation industry, including Joe Brumm, the Australian animator of Bluey fame, and Pierre Perifel, Director of Bad Guys, Anna has the industry's current stars on speed dial.[/vc_column_text][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column][vc_column][dfd_delimiter delimiter_style="dfd-delimiter-with-line" delimiter_border_style="dashed"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="2/3"][vc_column_text]

Jason Burns

  The client list of Jason Burns is also impressive. As an agent with UTA, as well, Jason Burns represents Joacquim Dos Santos Director of Spider-man: Across the Spider-verse, and Jorge Gutiérrez (Director of some of my favourite animated movies, including Maya and the Three and Book of Life). Since I'm already name-dropping, I might as well list out Jason's other clients. Kyle Balda and Robert Persichetti. So for any of you Directors-to-be of animated movies — Jason Burns is a name you'll want to know. Look at the output of just his clients in the animation business alone! The aforementioned movies + the Despicable Me series of films, The Incredibles, Wall-E 2, Toy Story 3, Shrek 2, and many more. Big movies with big-time animation talent.[/vc_column_text][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][dfd_single_image image="14233" image_size="custom" image_width="300" image_height="300" hover_style="dfd-image-scale" image_border_radius="10"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_delimiter delimiter_style="dfd-delimiter-with-line" delimiter_border_style="dashed"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][dfd_single_image image="14228" image_size="custom" image_width="300" image_height="300" hover_style="dfd-image-scale" image_border_radius="10"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="2/3"][vc_column_text]

Andrew Cannava

  Rounding out UTA's wide and deep bullpen of animation agents, Andrew Cannava is our third entry from the same agency. On the famous actor side of David's business, he's the agent for Elizabeth Banks. But don't let the long list of thespians among his clients dissuade you from looking at David for representation. He's the "guy" for such animators as Yarrow Cheney (Director of The Grinch) and Bobby Rubio (Pixar's Inside Out and Incredibles 2). Sandy Weinberg

February 23rd to March 3rd — Brussels, Belgium (in-person & virtual) Happy New Year! 2024 kicks off in Brussels. Anima is in its 43rd year, an impressive feat for an animation conference. But you can see why. The level of talent in Belgium and who this festival attracts internationally is second to none. No live-action animation, though. Anima focuses on animation created frame by frame, which can be traditional animated cartoons, stop-motion puppetry, or hand-animated plasticine models. May 25th, 26th — Berlin, Germany (onsite and virtually) Let's stay in Germany for the spring and head to the capital for an art experience that only Berlin can deliver. Donna Felton

June 9th to the 15th — Annecy, France (onsite and virtually) My top pick for the best animation conference in the world is no surprise: the Annecy Festival. Or the Festival d'Annecy. Or the more wordy Annecy International Animation Film Festival and Market. This is the conference every lover of animation should attend at least once in his or her lifetime. Why? It's the world's largest event dedicated to animation. It's in a lovely part of France. It's where the next generation of animators get their break. And it's an experience like no other. When animation is placed on such a pedestal, as only the French can do, you can only be swept away. The Annecy Festival has been going on for 60 years. The 2024 edition will have it all: massive screening to top-tier animation, workshops, and the Mifa, one the world's best places to do business both in person and virtually. If you've only got one event to go to, put this animation conference on your schedule.[/vc_column_text][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][vc_zigzag color="white" el_width="30"][ultimate_spacer height="20" height_on_tabs="20" height_on_tabs_portrait="20" height_on_mob_landscape="20" height_on_mob="20"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row css=".vc_custom_1696657907640{background-color: #edb39f !important;}"][vc_column][dfd_heading module_animation="transition.fadeIn" delimiter_style="icon" icon_size="32" style="style_01" icon="dfd-icon-medal_star dfd_icon_set-icon-medal_star" title_font_options="tag:h3|color:%23000000" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3" heading_margin="margin-top:20px;"]

screen_mobile_spacer_size="10"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text]Sensory gardens are an area of landscape architecture that is often overlooked in the thinking of project planners. Sensory gardens often have the main purpose of reducing stress, anxiety, and depression through sensory stimulation. These sensory gardens can be created through several methods. These methods use botanical color palettes, sculpture, and nature-inspired features in order to create a memorable sensory garden design.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text]There are designers who can help plan the concepts, visualizations, and eventual implementation of these sensory gardens. Sensory garden designers can come from many different types of backgrounds such as landscape architects, botanical artists, or horticulturists. Sensory garden designers are often hired for garden designs that are located in a public space, like a botanical park or kids' garden, or a private area such as a company courtyard.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" subtitle_font_options="tag:h3|font_family:QwigleyRegular"]Why are sensory gardens becoming popular?[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="10"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text]One of the reasons sensory gardens are becoming popular in public spaces, company courtyards, and botanical parks is that this type of garden has been proven to reduce stress, anxiety, and depression. The main senses for sensory gardens are sight, sound, and touch. For example, a tactile decision a sensory garden design might make is to play with humidity. The garden design audience could then feel the moisture and coolness in a tropical portion of the garden. Botanical experiences have also become popular in certain communities because sensory garden designers include specific plants for children with sensory processing disorders, autism, and sensory integration challenges.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text]Sensory processing disorder symptoms frequently include oversensitivity to sensory stimulation, under-sensitivity (hypersensitivity), or both. Children who suffer from sensory processing disorder can benefit greatly by spending time within sensory gardens designed specifically for sensory integration therapy. The sensory aspects of a garden design are just as important as the plants. For example, a sensory garden with beautiful blooms can be just as effective as sensory gardens that highlight sculptures and abstract artwork. A sensory garden should never contain sensory plants alone. There's more creativity to be had![/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" Hiring the Right Sensory Garden Designer Can Make All the Difference

[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="10"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text]Sensory gardens have been proven to reduce stress, anxiety, and depression through their use of color, art, and nature-inspired features. Increasingly, local governments, tourism centers, hospitals, corporate well-being centers, and botanical gardens are becoming interested in re-using existing spaces for sensory gardens. A well-designed sensory garden intends to affect people's calmness and attention to beauty.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text]Sensory gardens are created with many different types of plants such as flowers, shrubs, and ornamental trees. Oddtoe loves the geometry that's possible with topiary. In this way, you can create spaces of pure air in your sensory garden by using certain botanical shapes and voids in between these shapes. For example, you can design 'pockets' of space under certain tree species. Then an area is designed to feel serene by planting lots of cool-colored plants like bluebells.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="60" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="60" screen_tablet_spacer_size="50" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][dfd_delimiter delimiter_style="dfd-delimiter-with-icon" icon_size="15" delimiter_border_style="dotted" icon_fontawesome="fas fa-question-circle" show_icon="enable_icon" icon_color="#FFFFFF"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark" dfd_enable_overlay=""][vc_column width="1/4"][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/2"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="40" screen_tablet_spacer_size="40" screen_mobile_spacer_size="40"][vc_column_text item_animation="transition.fadeIn"]

Questions about

Sensory Garden Design?

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="40" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_accordion style="style-3" active_section="1" font_size="18" tab_title_google_fonts="yes" tab_title_custom_fonts="font_family:Arvo%3Aregular%2Citalic%2C700%2C700italic|font_style:700%20bold%20regular%3A700%3Anormal" icon_size="14"][vc_tta_section title="What are the reasons to get a sensory garden designed?" tab_id="1685677784578-172f9372-59216fce-87a64dfd-367fac06-a07f"][vc_column_text]

Sensory gardens certainly hold a lot of potential for a host of therapeutic reasons. However, there is one big, more simplistic reason why the world needs more of them: they're beautiful to relax in.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="What services does a sensory garden designer provide?" tab_id="1685677784323-438be9dd-da0e6fce-87a64dfd-367fac06-a07f"][vc_column_text]Oddtoe's sensory design service can include the thinking around materials such as bark, gravel, grasses, flowers, and shrubs; and features such as waterfalls, trails, and small ponds. This service seeks to: 1) enhance both the visual appeal of your land; 2) imagine the sounds and tactile experiences your audiences will have. Always with a focus on relaxation and contemplation. Oddtoe can guide you through selecting sensory plants that are best suited to your space – sensory gardens can be incorporated into public spaces such as city parks, museum courtyards and private gardens.[/vc_column_text][/vc_tta_section][vc_tta_section title="What does a sensory garden look like with global warming?" tab_id="1685677784395-526dd6ff-b9c26fce-87a64dfd-367fac06-a07f"][vc_column_text]

Drier climates will be the norm. Succulents and semi-arid topiary are a specialty in Oddtoe's southern hemisphere and Middle East work. In more moderate climates, irrigation systems and cold weather landscape needs are considered.

art, where creativity knows no bounds and the familiar transforms into the fantastical. AI digital art has greatly added to the body of weird art. (See generative AI's problems visualizing hands and feet.) Great weird art is an inside joke and an aesthetic. The appeal of it for me is its use in visual humor. For me, it takes inspiration from great and pretentious portraiture. It then blends itself with caricature and geometric shapes. Presto! You've got a captivating mix of illustration and character design. If weird art is what you seek, see the design of oddities here. This isn’t just about being different; it’s about challenging the norm, pushing the envelope, and embracing the unexpected. Here, geometric shapes take on lives of their own, transforming into surreal character studies, and into a next generation of visual storytelling.  Imagine a world where the natural elegance of design principles intertwines with the quirky, the odd, and the fantastical. [/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text]The inspiration behind these pieces? It comes from everywhere. The organic forms found in nature, the sleek lines of industrial design, the exaggerated features of caricature, and the whimsical nature of some sculptors —all contribute to creating art that’s as weird as it is wonderful. Picture geometric patterns with a grid of strange creatures or abstract designs that reveal hidden characters upon closer inspection. This is the essence of great art: it's always surprising, always intriguing. What sets this approach to weird art apart? It’s the fusion of tradition and innovation, the marriage of classic artistic techniques with cutting-edge technology. Using code, Oddtoe transforms ordinary shapes into extraordinary visions. These aren’t just static images; they’re immersive experiences that invite viewers to lose themselves in a world of oddities and marvels. In the world of weird art, there’s a playful unpredictability that keeps things exciting. WEIRD ART

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text]Each piece is a journey, an exploration of the bizarre and the beautiful. Imagine a geometric design morphing into a surreal landscape, or a weird sculpture that reveals hidden characters and stories upon closer inspection. It’s all about the thrill of discovery, the joy of the unexpected. Weird art is versatile, perfect for those who crave the unconventional. Looking to add some eccentric flair to your product design or visual marketing? Need unique illustrated concepts developed?  Seeking character designs that defy the ordinary? Oddtoe brings a touch of weirdness and wonder to any setting. Bold lines, a unique style , and intricate details come together to create pieces that are as eye-catching as they are thought-provoking. In an ever-evolving art scene, staying inspired means constantly experimenting with[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text]new techniques and technologies. By blending natural forms with the innovative possibilities of generative 3D geometry, this artist creates weird art that resonates with both traditionalists and modernists.  Each piece is a testament to the endless potential of creativity, a celebration of the strange and the sublime. Weird can also mean unique, a one-of-a-kind expression that stands out in a crowd. Embrace the odd, the peculiar, the extraordinary. It’s something to be proud of, a badge of honor in a world that often values conformity. So let's celebrate individuality, the courage to be different, and the beauty of uniqueness. So, whether an art enthusiast or someone with a penchant for the peculiar, this collection of weird art awaits. subtitle_responsive="line_height_mobile:28" subheading_margin="margin-bottom:10px;"]The Many Styles of Geometric Art[/dfd_heading][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text]Welcome to the wondrous world of geometric art, where the natural elegance of geometry meets the boundless creativity of life. This isn’t just art—it’s a celebration, an ode to the breathtaking forms that surround us. Inspired by the intricate patterns of Islamic art and the mesmerizing geometry found in nature, topiary, and industrial design, this new evolvement of an old human artform will be something unlike we've ever seen or experienced.  Geometry is everywhere. It’s in the delicate curves of a leaf, the spirals of a seashell, the structured beauty of a honeycomb. Each line, angle, and curve tells a story, whispering secrets about the world. This art is a homage to these natural wonders, capturing their essence through the lens of 3D geometry and patternwork. Every piece created is a love letter to the shapes and forms that inspire awe and wonder.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text]Imagine a world where every pattern is a glimpse into the design of nature. Geometric art isn’t just about creating visually stunning pieces; it’s about honoring the intricate dance of shapes that define the universe and then 'screwing it up.'. My inspiration comes from everywhere—the meticulous symmetry of Islamic tiles, the organic forms of topiary, the sleek lines of industrial design. Each artwork is a testament to the harmony and chaos, the simplicity and complexity of the world around. What makes this approach to geometric art special? Nothing really. I love it, because of the blend of tradition and innovation, the fusion of old-world charm and modern technology. Using algorithms and scripts (I don't write them), natural forms are transformed into immersive, 3D experiences. So yea, in summary, I see visual art and geometry as a deep dive into a very deep well of new creative forms. Perfect fun. [/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" Long live the sphere, the cube, & the torus...

GEOMETRIC ART

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="30" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="30" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text]There’s a playful side to this work as well. Art should evoke joy, curiosity, and a sense of wonder. Picture designing a traditional Islamic pattern suddenly coming alive with the organic shapes of nature. Imagine a geometric design that, upon closer inspection, reveals layers of complexity and hidden details. This playful unpredictability is at the heart of the artistic vision, making each piece a delightful journey of discovery. Geometric Art is versatile, just like the natural forms it celebrates. Bold lines, vibrant colors, intricate patterns—all come together to create pieces that stand out and make a statement. In a world that’s constantly changing, staying inspired is key. Oddtoe is an experiment with no end goal in mind. It's an exploration of new techniques and technologies, pushing the boundaries of what’s possible with geometric art, industrial design, and organic sculpture. [/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text]By blending the timeless beauty of natural forms with cutting-edge 3D geometry, the aim is to create art that resonates with both traditional art lovers and modern design enthusiasts. So, whether a seasoned art aficionado or someone who simply finds beauty in the world around them, this collection of Geometric Art awaits. Each piece is inspired by the natural shapes that surrounds us all. Dive into the world of 3D geometry, fractal design.  Let's see the next generation of patterns and construction. Let's see what modern tools and an artistic human can create. Join this journey through the enchanting realm of Geometric Art. These creations are ready to inspire and delight. Welcome to a place where nature’s beauty meets technological innovation, and where every pattern has a story to tell. Ready for a new style of visualization and geometric design?[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner][dfd_spacer Oddtoe's second city hub and a launching point for most American projects and commissions. As a visual artist specializing in 3D visualization, private garden design, and animation, Hollywood and Los Angeles as a whole are a hive of activity for what Oddtoe does. The city is home to the great animation studios like Disney, Warner Bros., Cartoon Network, and Dreamworks.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text]Los Angeles also boasts 263 sunny days per year, making it an ideal environment for the sustainable and imaginative gardens, the private and public landscapes designed in Oddtoe's studios. Finally, there's the practical side of the city's economy: industrial design. Southern California is a global center of 3D design: aerospace, movie & television prop making, and additive manufacturing.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="120" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_mobile_spacer_size="80" screen_normal_spacer_size="80" screen_tablet_spacer_size="80"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check="row-background-dark"][vc_column][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css="" item_animation="transition.fadeIn"]

Oddtoe is dedicated to transforming artistic visions into reality, capturing [/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/4"][vc_column_text]the essence of the dreamers who made Los Angeles the global center of creativity. width="1/4"][vc_column_text]Oddtoe continues the fine tradition of Australian design, visualization, & animation. Oddtoe is based out of Melbourne, Australia, with an additional presence in Los Angeles and Berlin. Oddtoe is at heart a visualizer and visual storyteller. Date Night Confessionals is a new animation series. Dare I say it's unsympathetic to the dating scene as it appears today. [vc_row][vc_column width="1/4"][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/2"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][dfd_delimiter delimiter_style="dfd-delimiter-with-text" text_delimiter="Mirth in Your Face" delimiter_border_style="dotted" custom_fonts="font_family:Qwigley%3Aregular|font_style:400%20regular%3A400%3Anormal" module_animation="transition.expandIn" use_google_fonts="show" title_font_options="font_size:30|line_height:38"][vc_single_image image="16107" img_size="full" add_caption="yes" alignment="center" style="vc_box_shadow_3d" css="" onclick="link_one_page" item_animation="transition.fadeIn" title="Oddtoe the Datalabs Agency on YouTube"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][vc_column_text css=""]

I like data. Do I love it, though?! — as in, do I sit on a beach and parse spreadsheets of zeros and ones? Nah. I've made a living running the Datalabs Agency for a decade or so. Big projects, visualizing data in interactive websites, analytics dashboards, and all kinds of video, online, and flat image forms. 

Then I've got this brand or what I call my artistic love affair, Oddtoe. I don't have to be PC. I can illustrate, caricature, and spoof my way into whatever topic I want. I think of a joke, something that amuses me and I can design it and push that idea out into the world safely. Except for a few years when I worked at National Geographic, I've had a 'firewall' between my professional life and my artistic one.

Not anymore. I'm bored with playing it safe. I realize I've got an opportunity to not give a crap as to what a corporate HR executive will 'action' once he or she sees 'moderately off-brand material' on my other site. ;)[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][dfd_delimiter delimiter_style="dfd-delimiter-with-text" text_delimiter="Spermtoe & the Bubble Brain in a Beaker" delimiter_border_style="dotted" custom_fonts="font_family:Qwigley%3Aregular|font_style:400%20regular%3A400%3Anormal" module_animation="transition.expandIn" use_google_fonts="show" title_font_options="font_size:30|line_height:38"][vc_single_image image="16108" img_size="full" add_caption="yes" alignment="center" style="vc_box_shadow_3d" css="" onclick="link_one_page" item_animation="transition.fadeIn" title="Co-branded Content"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]

First off, as a solo visualizer/cartoonist/animator, I've always been jealous of musicians and their ability to jam with others. To come up with album and song titles. To name their bands. So this merger of my work (at least on YouTube) starts with a band name: Oddtoe & the Datalabs Agency.

So what does a merger of Oddtoe & the Datalabs Agency look like? Two things: 1) That's a really good question. 2) Stop being so nosy. 

All advice leads to designing new types of animation and data-driven storytelling. As my great-grandmother used to say: "The best way to figure out where you want to go in life is by designing YouTube thumbnails."[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_delimiter delimiter_style="dfd-delimiter-with-text" text_delimiter="Thumbnail A" delimiter_border_style="dotted" custom_fonts="font_family:Qwigley%3Aregular|font_style:400%20regular%3A400%3Anormal" module_animation="transition.expandIn" use_google_fonts="show" title_font_options="font_size:30|line_height:38"][vc_single_image image="16109" img_size="full" add_caption="yes" alignment="center" style="vc_box_shadow_3d" css="" onclick="link_one_page" item_animation="transition.fadeIn" title="Absurd Influencers"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][vc_column_text css=""]

I don't want to put my face in places where it does not belong. But I'm in these thumbnails. With the onset of AI video slop that I want to steer away from, I heard that having you — your human-ness shown in your thumbnail — that gets more engagement.

Avatar head? Check. I love a giant-sized font. These thumbnails got that...Check. And the image has to be quirky — weird angle, maybe a "What the #$%^!" is that?! kind of shock value. Check. Essentially, I ask myself: Can I trick some gullible person to pause their life, click on my thumbnail, and entrust their limited intelligence to me? Check.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner][dfd_delimiter delimiter_style="dfd-delimiter-with-text" text_delimiter="Thumbnail B" delimiter_border_style="dotted" custom_fonts="font_family:Qwigley%3Aregular|font_style:400%20regular%3A400%3Anormal" module_animation="transition.expandIn" use_google_fonts="show" title_font_options="font_size:30|line_height:38"][vc_single_image image="16111" img_size="full" add_caption="yes" alignment="center" style="vc_box_shadow_3d" img_link_target="_blank" css="" onclick="img_link_large" title="World-Class Dipshits"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][vc_column_text css=""]

So I designed up two thumbnails. Hand-crafted, artisanal thumbnails to get the ball rolling. I've set up to start filming this week. So, subscribe to my new Oddtoe & the Datalabs Agency YouTube channel and get on board at the ground level.

Any topics or subjects you want me to tackle? Get in touch with me — love hearing new ideas that I will most likely ignore.

Just kidding. But, I'm not...

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/4"][/vc_column][/vc_row]

posts/14493.title: Oddtoe's Studios in Australia
posts/14493.content:
[vc_row][vc_column width="1/4"][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/2"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][dfd_delimiter delimiter_style="dfd-delimiter-with-text" text_delimiter="Offices Over the Years" delimiter_border_style="dotted" custom_fonts="font_family:Qwigley%3Aregular|font_style:400%20regular%3A400%3Anormal" module_animation="transition.expandIn" use_google_fonts="show" title_font_options="font_size:30|line_height:38"][vc_single_image image="13222" img_size="full" add_caption="yes" alignment="center" style="vc_box_shadow_3d" css="" onclick="link_one_page" item_animation="transition.fadeIn" title="Oddtoe's Studios in Australia"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][vc_column_text css=""]

I live in Australia. I swapped the icy streets of Capitol Hill in Washington, DC in December of 2006. (Winter becomes summer if you sit on an aeroplane long enough.)

Being an artist in the Southern Hemisphere — in Melbourne, Australia to be exact — has professional advantages. One of those advantages is designing and animating in office locations I would never have thought I'd work in. Fixed sites like an abandoned gunpowder factory from the 1880s gold rush era in the Australian state of Victoria. And I take my work on the road with me now — kangaroos and the occasional koala are who I choose to surround myself with. Here are my top 5 locations where I, as Oddtoe, have worked from.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][dfd_delimiter delimiter_style="dfd-delimiter-with-text" text_delimiter="Along the River" delimiter_border_style="dotted" custom_fonts="font_family:Qwigley%3Aregular|font_style:400%20regular%3A400%3Anormal" module_animation="transition.expandIn" use_google_fonts="show" title_font_options="font_size:30|line_height:38"][vc_single_image image="12624" img_size="full" add_caption="yes" alignment="center" style="vc_box_shadow_3d" css="" onclick="link_one_page" item_animation="transition.fadeIn" title="Whiskey Hill on the Maribyrnong"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][vc_column_text css=""]

Two rivers run through Melbourne: the Yarra and the Maribyrnong. On the banks of the mighty Maribyrnong, I had my home office — a quiet, ground-level basement space with a green-grass lawn and palm trees, was on the other side of a glass door.. 

A favourite space of mine on this list, because my kids would come down into my home studio and learn the art of goofing off from an expert. I learned a lot, too. During this period, I took on some notable clients, ones from Saudi Arabia (NEOM), the US (BlackRock, Lockheed Martin, Intel), Asia (Marriott) and Europe (Mercedes-Benz) in this space. Best feature of this studio? My then twelve-year-old daughter sorted a wall of book according to colour— the best Zoom background. She received numerous compliments from clients. And I, in turn, looked grossly more educated than I really am...[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][dfd_delimiter delimiter_style="dfd-delimiter-with-text" text_delimiter="Australia in the Betty White Van" delimiter_border_style="dotted" custom_fonts="font_family:Qwigley%3Aregular|font_style:400%20regular%3A400%3Anormal" module_animation="transition.expandIn" use_google_fonts="show" title_font_options="font_size:30|line_height:38"][vc_single_image image="15911" img_size="full" add_caption="yes" alignment="center" style="vc_box_shadow_3d" css="" onclick="link_one_page" item_animation="transition.fadeIn" title="Vanlife in Oz"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][vc_column_text css=""]

Is it a bucket item to work alongside the ocean surrounded by kangaroo droppings? Maybe half of that work experience is. When a strong wifi signal isn't a priority, I take Oddtoe on the road. My mobile office — one that I work in at least once a month — consists of a van hauling a small camper trailer.

Betty White Van has a computer monitor, bed, and solar panels. The tiny camper trailer I have hauling is an Avan, an a-frame pop-up trailer that sports a fridge, a sink, electrical chargers, a table, and a bed. Best trips in this 'office'?: Robe, South Australia, Lorne & Wye River (the Great Ocean Road in Victoria), and a few trips to the Grampians. Next trip in 2025?: To the nation's capitol, Canberra, for a government data and analytics conference. Think: staying in a campground in the forest; and 'Clark Kent-ing' into a suit to schmooze policy wonks at a convention centre. I love that night and day difference.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][vc_row_inner][vc_column_inner][dfd_delimiter delimiter_style="dfd-delimiter-with-text" text_delimiter="Warehouse Studio in Fitzroy" delimiter_border_style="dotted" custom_fonts="font_family:Qwigley%3Aregular|font_style:400%20regular%3A400%3Anormal" module_animation="transition.expandIn" use_google_fonts="show" title_font_options="font_size:30|line_height:38"][vc_single_image image="14531" img_size="full" add_caption="yes" alignment="center" style="vc_box_shadow_3d" img_link_target="_blank" css="" onclick="img_link_large" title="Welcome to Hipster-ville"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][vc_column_text css=""]

Fitzroy, a neighbourhood just north of Melbourne, is a centre of excellence in hipster-dom. Handlebar moustaches, beetle-excrement fair-trade coffee, and every-fucking-thing is artisanal.

I put my company right in the centre of it all, in a four-story, old fruit-and-veg warehouse just off the main shopping district: Brunswick Street. Many of my past employees will remember this as their office. Best feature of the Fitzroy studio?: For one-on-one catch-ups with staff members, I'd sometimes take them to a cafe or restaurant for a coffee. The rooftop at a place called Naked for Satan was a favourite. But was often a confusing subject lines in my emails for employees who'd never heard of it — "Meeting: Naked for Satan".[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/4"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column width="1/4"][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/2"][dfd_delimiter delimiter_style="dfd-delimiter-with-text" text_delimiter="Nugget of Gratitude..." delimiter_border_style="dotted" custom_fonts="font_family:Qwigley%3Aregular|font_style:400%20regular%3A400%3Anormal" module_animation="transition.expandIn" use_google_fonts="show" title_font_options="font_size:30|line_height:38"][vc_single_image image="13194" img_size="full" add_caption="yes" alignment="center" style="vc_box_shadow_3d" css_animation="fadeIn" onclick="zoom" title="Jack's Magazine"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][vc_column_text css=""]

Wow. I loved working here. Are you allowed to have fond memories of the Pandemic?! Of course, you are (if you were lucky to have them.)

Jack's Magazine is a funny name for what was an abandoned gunpowder factory from the 1880s. Located up the Maribyrnong River from Melbourne, Australia, Jack's Magazine was the place to be if you wanted to blow shit up and get rich doing it. Remember: this was peak gold rush time in a city that was, for a brief time, the wealthiest place on Earth. I, however, moved in some one hundred and forty years after that. Again, I put my company right in the centre of a 5-acre "campus" of blue stone buildings, the only person and business within its walls. The place had ghosts at night and the cheekiest fox roaming the blast mounds of park during the day. Best memory at Jack's Magazine?: March 2020 was just after the big bushfires in Australia and at the start of the world-wide Covid-19 pandemic. I home-schooled my kids inside the three-metre-high walls of this fort. Cinematically, I was imagining the zombie apocalypse was unfolding and simultaneously I was receiving 'Father of the Year' honors. What other dad was able to secure a site like this one for raising children as society unraveled? In reality, it was a beautiful time — my two kids and I doing arts & crafts & homework & game design & rockclimbing...[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][dfd_delimiter icon_size="13" delimiter_border_style="dotted" icon_fontawesome="fas fa-industry" icon_color="#f9f9f9" icon_hover_color="#969696" content_bg_color="#232300" content_bg_hover_color="#827306" delim_circle_line_color="#232323" delim_hover_circle_line_color="#636363" show_icon="enable_icon"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][vc_column_text css=""]

Is that all? No. I missed two of other notable places in my life:

  • The Art Deco office I purchased in the Manchester Unity Building is across from Melbourne's City Hall.
  • A Mongolian yurt that formed part of a Washington, DC puppetry centre in Glen Echo Park, across the river from the C.I.A.
Another blog post, perhaps. Thanks for reading.[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][vc_hoverbox image="13738" primary_title="Projection Art" hover_title="Projection Artist" hover_title_use_theme_fonts="yes" hover_title_css_animation="none" hover_background_color="custom" use_custom_fonts_hover_title="true" hover_custom_background="rgba(97,124,62,0.38)" hover_title_link="url:https%3A%2F%2Fwww.oddtoe.com%2Fartist-designer%2Fprojection-artist%2F|title:Projection%20Artist"]Events are always better with nighttime entertainment. Projection and animation are the perfect way to get your audience on their feet.[/vc_hoverbox][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="10" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="10" screen_tablet_spacer_size="10" screen_mobile_spacer_size="5"][vc_column_text css=""]

What does Oddtoe do? For one thing: he's a projection artist.

[/vc_column_text][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="15" screen_mobile_spacer_size="19"][vc_single_image image="11978" img_size="50x50" alignment="center" style="vc_box_shadow_border_circle_2" css=".vc_custom_1717584262883{border-radius: 3px !important;}" item_animation="transition.fadeIn"][dfd_spacer screen_wide_resolution="1280" screen_wide_spacer_size="20" screen_normal_resolution="1024" screen_tablet_resolution="800" screen_mobile_resolution="480" screen_normal_spacer_size="20" screen_tablet_spacer_size="20" screen_mobile_spacer_size="20"][/vc_column][vc_column width="1/4"][/vc_column][/vc_row]
